meta.name: Screen and triage job applications with Gemini, Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail

name: AI ATS + Resume Screening + Recruiter Workflow Automation

parameters.content:
## AI ATS + Resume Screening + Recruiter Workflow Automation

### How it works

This workflow automates candidate intake, resume screening, and recruiter follow-up for an ATS process. It accepts applications from a form, validates and deduplicates submissions, extracts resume text, evaluates candidates with an AI model, logs results to Google Sheets, and routes notifications or emails based on the final status. A separate Slack-triggered path helps recruiters schedule shortlisted candidate interviews, while an error workflow alerts the team when executions fail.

### Setup steps

- Configure the form trigger with the required candidate fields and resume file upload field expected by the extraction step.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and update sheet IDs, tab names, and columns for application logs, invalid submissions, duplicates, and unparsed resumes.
- Configure the Job Config node with the target job title, job description, shortlist score, and manual review score thresholds.
- Set up the AI HTTP request credentials or API key for the Gemini/Generative Language endpoint used by the candidate evaluation step.
- Connect Slack credentials and set the correct recruiter, hiring team, duplicate, invalid submission, and error alert channels.
- Connect Gmail credentials for rejection, resume re-upload, and shortlist/interview emails.
- Connect Google Calendar credentials and choose the calendar used for availability checks and interview event creation.

### Customization

Adjust the job description, scoring thresholds, Slack routing, email templates, calendar duration, and AI evaluation prompt to match each role or recruiting process.

## Receive and configure application

Starts the application flow from a form submission, assigns an application ID and timestamp, loads job screening settings, and validates whether the submission has the required information.

## Validate and deduplicate submission

Handles the validation outcomes in the nearby branch cluster: invalid submissions are logged and sent to admins, while valid submissions are checked for duplicates before either notifying the recruiter or preparing the resume field for parsing.

## Extract resume text

Extracts text from the uploaded resume file and checks whether the resume content was successfully parsed before sending it to AI screening.

## Handle parse failure

Logs resumes that could not be parsed and emails the candidate to request a corrected or re-uploaded resume.

## Evaluate candidate with AI

Sends parsed resume content and job context to the AI model, parses the returned evaluation, and derives the candidate's final screening status.

## Log and route result

Stores the evaluated application in Google Sheets and switches execution to the appropriate downstream action based on the final candidate status.

## Manual review alert

Notifies the recruiter when an application needs manual review rather than automatic acceptance or rejection.

## Shortlist team alert

Alerts the hiring team about candidates who meet the shortlist criteria.

## Recruiter review FYI

Sends an informational Slack notification to the recruiter for candidates in the review band.

## Send rejection email

Emails candidates who do not meet the screening threshold with a rejection message.

## Slack request intake

Starts the recruiter automation path from a Slack event and filters whether the message should be processed.

## Thread analysis and routing

Fetches the Slack message thread, analyzes it with custom JavaScript, and routes the request based on detected intent or required conditions.

## Schedule interview and email

Checks Google Calendar for busy times, computes an available interview slot, creates the calendar event, and sends the shortlist email to the candidate.

## Workflow error alerting

Captures workflow execution errors, formats the failed workflow and node details, and sends an alert to the team in Slack.

parameters.formDescription: Apply for this role. Attach your resume as PDF or DOCX.

nodes.name: Set Application ID and Date
nodes.notes: Every applicant gets a stable applicationId here, before anything else runs. Every downstream node that needs it (logging, Slack, email, the reaction-approval callback) pulls it explicitly via $('Generate Application ID').item.json.applicationId rather than relying on pass-through, so it can never get silently dropped by a node that replaces $json (e.g. a Sheets read or an HTTP Request).

nodes.name: Set Job Configuration
nodes.notes: Edit jobTitle / jobDescription / shortlistScore / reviewScore per role. Nothing downstream needs to change.

assignments.name: jobDescription
assignments.value: EDIT ME PER ROLE: 4+ years React, TypeScript, state management (Redux/Zustand), REST/GraphQL API integration, strong CSS/responsive design, comfortable in an agile team.

nodes.name: Append Invalid Submission to Sheets
nodes.notes: Rejected_Invalid sheet header row: ApplicationId, SubmittedAt, Name, Email, Reason. Pulls ApplicationId from $('Generate Application ID').item.json.applicationId so every rejected/invalid submission is still traceable.

parameters.text: =⚠️ Malformed application submission (ID: {{ $('Set Application ID and Date').item.json.applicationId }}) from *{{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Email'] }}* — missing/invalid email or no resume attached. Skipped automatically.

nodes.name: Check Duplicate in Sheets
nodes.notes: Reads the Applicants sheet filtered by Email (configure the filter in the node UI — field name depends on your n8n version). Recommend also enabling 'Always Output Data' in node Settings so a zero-match result still produces one empty item and doesn't silently stall the branch.

parameters.text: =🔁 Duplicate application detected (ID: {{ $('Set Application ID and Date').item.json.applicationId }}) from *{{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Full Name'] }}* ({{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Email'] }}). No new evaluation was run.

nodes.name: Extract Text from Resume
nodes.notes: If your form's file field produces a different binary key than 'Resume', check the item's binary tab and update this.

nodes.name: Log Unparsed Resume to Sheets
nodes.notes: Also logs ApplicationId (from Generate Application ID) alongside Name/Email for traceability.

parameters.message:
=Hi {{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Full Name'] }},

We received your application (reference {{ $('Set Application ID and Date').item.json.applicationId }}) but weren't able to read your resume file — it may be a scanned image or a corrupted upload. Could you reply with a text-based PDF or DOCX version?

Best,
Recruiting Team
parameters.subject: We couldn't process your resume

nodes.name: Post to AI Evaluation API
nodes.notes: Single Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite call that replaces the old 3-call chain (profile extraction + fit scoring + red-flag screening). One request instead of three cuts token spend roughly 3x and removes two extra points of failure/latency. retryOnFail is set so a transient 429/5xx doesn't fail the whole run.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: 'You are an expert technical recruiter. Do all of the following in one pass, using ONLY evidence found in the resume text below — never invent facts.

ROLE: ' + $('Set Job Configuration').item.json.jobTitle + '
JOB DESCRIPTION / REQUIREMENTS: ' + $('Set Job Configuration').item.json.jobDescription + '

TASKS:
1) Extract a structured profile: every distinct skill/technology mentioned, total years of professional experience as a number, highest education level, and past employer names.
2) Score the candidate 0-100 for fit against the role above, and classify as Shortlist (score at or above ' + $('Set Job Configuration').item.json.shortlistScore + '), Review (score at or above ' + $('Set Job Configuration').item.json.reviewScore + '), or Reject (below that). Base the summary strictly on resume evidence.
3) Screen for red flags only (do not let this affect the fit score itself): unexplained employment gaps over 6 months, vague or inflated titles, inconsistent or overlapping dates, and generic templated language suggesting a mass-application spray. Classify overall risk as Low, Medium, or High and list the specific flags found (empty array if none).

RESUME TEXT: ' + $json.text }] }], generationConfig: { responseMimeType: 'application/json', responseSchema: { type: 'OBJECT', properties: { skills: { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'STRING' } }, yearsExperience: { type: 'NUMBER' }, education: { type: 'STRING' }, pastEmployers: { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'STRING' } }, score: { type: 'NUMBER' }, recommendation: { type: 'STRING', enum: ['Shortlist','Review','Reject'] }, summary: { type: 'STRING' }, riskLevel: { type: 'STRING', enum: ['Low','Medium','High'] }, flags: { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'STRING' } } }, required: ['skills','yearsExperience','education','pastEmployers','score','recommendation','summary','riskLevel','flags'] } } }) }}

nodes.name: Parse AI Response
nodes.notes: Centralizes JSON.parse in one try/catch instead of the fragile pattern of repeating JSON.parse(...) inside many separate Set-node expressions (where one malformed field throws and kills the whole item). On failure it doesn't drop the applicant — it forces riskLevel='High', which routes them to Manual Review below.

nodes.name: Record Applicant Status in Sheets
nodes.notes: Applicants sheet header row: ApplicationId, SubmittedAt, Name, Email, LinkedIn, Skills, YearsExperience, Education, PastEmployers, Score, Recommendation, RiskLevel, Flags, FinalStatus, SlackChannel, SlackMessageTs, DecidedBy, DecidedAt, Notes. ApplicationId is the primary key every later lookup/update (duplicate check, Slack-reaction approval, weekly digest) keys off of.

nodes.name: Alert Recruiter for Manual Review
nodes.notes: Approval now happens by emoji reaction on THIS message, not by Block Kit buttons/webhook. This node's output must include the posted message's `ts` and `channel` so the next node can save them — field names vary slightly by n8n version, so open the node's output once after a test run and confirm (commonly $json.ts / $json.channel, sometimes nested under $json.message).

parameters.text: =🟡 *Borderline candidate logged (ID {{ $json.applicationId }}):* {{ $json.name }} (Score: {{ $json.score }}/100) — recommendation: Review. No action needed unless you want to override.
